import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
cameras = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a bar chart to show the distribution of cameras by brand
brand_counts = cameras['brand'].value_counts()
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.countplot(x='brand', data=cameras)
plt.title('Camera Brands')
plt.xlabel('Brand')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a scatter plot to show the relationship between megapixels and price
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.scatterplot(x='megapixels', y='price_usd', data=cameras)
plt.title('Megapixels vs Price')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels')
plt.ylabel('Price ($USD)')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output2.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a histogram to show the distribution of camera prices
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.histplot(cameras['price_usd'], kde=True)
plt.title('Distribution of Camera Prices')
plt.xlabel('Price ($USD)')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output3.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
